producer_report.summary: Each cold build in `athena measure-build` now records peak resident memory and cores used. `BuildMeasurement` has four new optional fields: first and second peak resident bytes, and first and second cores used. Old records still parse, because the fields are optional with serde defaults. `validate()` rejects negative or non-finite values. `athena status` prints the figures on the build line. I re-ran only the disk tests in this round, and they pass. The earlier-round work on records, status, CLI tests, docs and CHANGELOG is still in place, and I did not re-run its tests this round.

criteria_check.criterion: BuildMeasurement in crates/athena-data/src/records.rs gains optional peak-resident-memory and cores-used fields with serde defaults, and validate() rejects negative or non-finite values.
criteria_check.evidence: Done in the earlier round. I did not re-read or re-run it this round.

criteria_check.criterion: BuildRun and CargoBuild::build in crates/athena-core/src/disk.rs capture peak resident memory and cores used of each cold build from the cargo process, and measure_build stores them in the record.
criteria_check.evidence: disk.rs has BuildRun.peak_resident_bytes and BuildRun.cores_used, with cores computed as CPU seconds divided by wall seconds (about lines 795-892). measure_build copies them into the record's first_* and second_* fields (about lines 1073-1076).

criteria_check.criterion: A test parses a JSON build-measurement record written without the new fields and it deserializes with those fields None; a test round-trips a record with them set. Run `cargo test -p athena-data`.
criteria_check.evidence: Tests added in the earlier round. I did not re-run `cargo test -p athena-data` this round.

criteria_check.criterion: build_measurement_line prints the peak memory and cores when present and still prints old records without them; tests in status.rs and crates/athena-cli/tests/status_build_measurement.rs check the printed text. Run `cargo test -p athena-core -p athena-cli`.
criteria_check.evidence: Done in the earlier round. This round I ran only `cargo test -p athena-core disk`.

criteria_check.criterion: A disk.rs test with a fake builder checks measure_build writes the builder's memory and core figures into the committed record. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
criteria_check.evidence: The fake builder returns PEAK_BYTES[n] and CORES[n] (disk.rs around line 1583). measure_build_writes_t_s_both_times_and_the_cache_counts asserts that both the returned record and the committed record (read back by `measurements(&athena)`) hold those four values (lines 1651-1657). `cargo test -p athena-core disk` passed all 37 tests.

criteria_check.criterion: `cargo test` passes for the workspace and `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.
The design doc docs/design/agent-and-build-slots.md or CHANGELOG.md notes the new fields briefly, if the repository convention records such changes.
